target.name: obsolete renal control of peripheral vascular resistance involved in regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure
target.description: Long-term arterial blood pressure is set largely by the kidney, which adjusts the tone of peripheral resistance vessels and thereby the force opposing blood flow. This renal contribution to peripheral vascular resistance is built around angiotensinogen, the liver-derived precursor cleaved to angiotensin II, which constricts arterioles through the type 1 receptor and raises systemic pressure, while the type 2 receptor and the MAS1 receptor for angiotensin-(1-7) oppose that action with vasodilation.

target.name: regulation of synaptic vesicle priming
target.description: Before a synaptic vesicle can release neurotransmitter it must be made fusion-competent, and this pathway tunes how many vesicles reach that primed, release-ready state. Because priming sets the size of the readily releasable pool, its regulation determines release probability, short-term plasticity and the fidelity of fast synaptic transmission; loss of the machinery produces severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathies and movement disorders.

target.description: Growth, survival and migration signals delivered through EGFR-family receptors are tuned upward by this set of activators, which raises the frequency or amplitude of ERBB signalling and thereby the proliferative output that epithelial tissues depend on for repair and that carcinomas exploit. Several routes converge on the receptors: ADAM17 sheds membrane-anchored ligands such as TGF-alpha and amphiregulin to make them available, proteases and the urokinase receptor system remodel the pericellular environment, and G protein-coupled receptors including GPER1 transactivate the pathway.

target.description: DNA lesions block the replicative polymerases, and this step is how a stalled fork registers that fact and hands the template to a polymerase that can copy past damage. It matters because a fork arrested at a lesion will collapse into double-strand breaks unless replication is allowed to continue, and because the switch it triggers is inherently mutagenic, shaping the mutation spectra seen in tumours.

Together these activities set the cell's capacity for ribosome biogenesis and accurate mRNA output, and hence growth and protein synthesis.
